newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean processing hit by trade protest.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean processing hit by trade protest.

text.p: India's soybean processors are working at less than 10 percent of capacity due to a trade protest, dealers said on Tuesday.
All major soybean markets in the central state of Madhya Pradesh were shut with traders on strike for the past week in protest against the imposition of a local government market tax, they said.
The processing plants were also affected by their lack of stocks.
Indian soymeal was in short supply with only a small quantity traded during the week.
Soymeal was quoted at $326-327 per tonne FAS (free alongside ship) for west coast ports, compared with $261-262 per tonne at the same time last year.
Traders said soybeans were quoted at 13,550-13,650 rupees per tonne in plant delivery condition against 9,200-9,400 rupees per tonne at the start of the season in November.
Indian rapeseed extraction was in good demand with around 15,000 tonnes traded in the last week of April.
